"""
Classify MuJoCo geoms into semantic categories for occupancy labeling.

Categories:
  0 = free (background)
  1 = table
  2 = robot
  3 = target object
"""

import re

FREE = 0
TABLE = 1
ROBOT = 2
TARGET = 3

CATEGORY_NAMES = {FREE: "free", TABLE: "table", ROBOT: "robot", TARGET: "target"}

# Patterns matched against geom names (case-insensitive)
ROBOT_PATTERNS = [
    r"robot\d*",
    r"gripper",
    r"finger",
    r"link\d*",
    r"hand",
    r"panda",
    r"mount",
]

TABLE_PATTERNS = [
    r"table",
    r"arena",
    r"floor",
]

# Geoms to always skip (visual-only, ground plane, etc.)
SKIP_PATTERNS = [
    r"^$",  # unnamed
    r"floor",
    r"ground",
]


def classify_geom(geom_name, body_name, geom_type):
    """Classify a single geom into a semantic category.

    Returns:
        int category, or None to skip this geom (ground plane, visual-only)
    """
    if geom_name is None:
        geom_name = ""
    if body_name is None:
        body_name = ""

    gn = geom_name.lower()
    bn = body_name.lower()

    # Skip ground plane (type 0 = PLANE)
    if geom_type == 0:
        return None

    # Robot parts: match on geom name or body name
    for pat in ROBOT_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return ROBOT

    # Table / arena
    for pat in TABLE_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return TABLE

    # Everything else is a target object
    return TARGET


def build_geom_class_map(sim):
    """Build geom_id -> semantic_class mapping for all geoms in the model.

    Args:
        sim: robosuite MjSim instance

    Returns:
        dict[int, int]: geom_id -> semantic category (0-3)
        Geoms that should be skipped are not included.
    """
    model = sim.model
    geom_map = {}

    for i in range(model.ngeom):
        geom_name = model.geom_id2name(i)
        body_id = model.geom_bodyid[i]
        body_name = model.body_id2name(body_id)
        geom_type = model.geom_type[i]

        cat = classify_geom(geom_name, body_name, geom_type)
        if cat is not None:
            geom_map[i] = cat

    return geom_map


def print_geom_classification(sim, geom_map):
    """Debug helper: print all geom classifications."""
    model = sim.model
    data = sim.data

    type_names = {
        0: "PLANE", 1: "HFIELD", 2: "SPHERE", 3: "CAPSULE",
        4: "ELLIPSOID", 5: "CYLINDER", 6: "BOX", 7: "MESH",
    }

    for i in range(model.ngeom):
        geom_name = model.geom_id2name(i) or f"unnamed_{i}"
        body_id = model.geom_bodyid[i]
        body_name = model.body_id2name(body_id) or f"body_{body_id}"
        geom_type = model.geom_type[i]
        pos = data.geom_xpos[i]
        cat = geom_map.get(i, None)
        cat_str = CATEGORY_NAMES.get(cat, "SKIP") if cat is not None else "SKIP"
        tname = type_names.get(geom_type, f"UNK({geom_type})")

        print(
            f"g[{i:3d}] {geom_name:45s} body={body_name:35s} "
            f"type={tname:8s} cat={cat_str:8s} "
            f"pos=[{pos[0]:.3f},{pos[1]:.3f},{pos[2]:.3f}]"
        )

"""
Classify MuJoCo geoms into semantic categories for occupancy labeling.

Categories:
  0 = free (background)
  1 = table
  2 = robot
  3 = target object
"""

import re

FREE = 0
TABLE = 1
ROBOT = 2
TARGET = 3

CATEGORY_NAMES = {FREE: "free", TABLE: "table", ROBOT: "robot", TARGET: "target"}

# Patterns matched against geom names (case-insensitive)
ROBOT_PATTERNS = [
    r"robot\d*",
    r"gripper",
    r"finger",
    r"link\d*",
    r"hand",
    r"panda",
    r"mount",
]

TABLE_PATTERNS = [
    r"table",
    r"wooden_cabinet",
    r"flat_stove",
    r"cabinet",
    r"stove",
    r"microwave",
    r"fridge",
]

SKIP_PATTERNS = [
    r"wall",
    r"floor",
    r"ground",
    r"arena",
]


def classify_geom(geom_name, body_name, geom_type):
    if geom_name is None:
        geom_name = ""
    if body_name is None:
        body_name = ""

    gn = geom_name.lower()
    bn = body_name.lower()

    if geom_type == 0:
        return None

    for pat in SKIP_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return None

    if bn == "world":
        return None

    for pat in ROBOT_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return ROBOT

    for pat in TABLE_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return TABLE

    return TARGET


def build_geom_class_map(sim):
    """Build geom_id -> semantic_class mapping for all geoms in the model.

    Args:
        sim: robosuite MjSim instance

    Returns:
        dict[int, int]: geom_id -> semantic category (0-3)
        Geoms that should be skipped are not included.
    """
    model = sim.model
    geom_map = {}

    for i in range(model.ngeom):
        geom_name = model.geom_id2name(i)
        body_id = model.geom_bodyid[i]
        body_name = model.body_id2name(body_id)
        geom_type = model.geom_type[i]

        cat = classify_geom(geom_name, body_name, geom_type)
        if cat is not None:
            geom_map[i] = cat

    return geom_map


def print_geom_classification(sim, geom_map):
    """Debug helper: print all geom classifications."""
    model = sim.model
    data = sim.data

    type_names = {
        0: "PLANE", 1: "HFIELD", 2: "SPHERE", 3: "CAPSULE",
        4: "ELLIPSOID", 5: "CYLINDER", 6: "BOX", 7: "MESH",
    }

    for i in range(model.ngeom):
        geom_name = model.geom_id2name(i) or f"unnamed_{i}"
        body_id = model.geom_bodyid[i]
        body_name = model.body_id2name(body_id) or f"body_{body_id}"
        geom_type = model.geom_type[i]
        pos = data.geom_xpos[i]
        cat = geom_map.get(i, None)
        cat_str = CATEGORY_NAMES.get(cat, "SKIP") if cat is not None else "SKIP"
        tname = type_names.get(geom_type, f"UNK({geom_type})")

        print(
            f"g[{i:3d}] {geom_name:45s} body={body_name:35s} "
            f"type={tname:8s} cat={cat_str:8s} "
            f"pos=[{pos[0]:.3f},{pos[1]:.3f},{pos[2]:.3f}]"
        )
PYEOF

The problem is clear: `mesh.contains(local)` is very expensive - it uses ray casting for each point. For 264 geoms, many of which are MESH type, this would be extremely slow.

Two key optimizations:
1. **Skip visual geoms**: In MuJoCo, visual and collision geoms are in different groups. Visual geoms (geom_group=0 or 1) just for rendering, collision geoms (group with contype/conaffinity) are for physics. For occupancy, we only need collision geoms or a representative set.

Actually wait, the issue is more nuanced. 

In robosuite, the naming convention makes this clear: geoms with `_vis` suffix are purely visual, while `_collision` suffix marks collision geometry. The robot has far more visual geoms than collision ones - each link has multiple visual mesh geoms but only a single collision mesh. Looking at the explore output, there are about 50 visual mesh geoms for the robot arm alone, plus another 16 for the gripper, but only 8 collision geoms for the links and a handful more for the gripper. So I can filter out all the `_vis` geoms and focus only on collision geometry, which should dramatically reduce the number of expensive containment checks.

The collision geoms are still mesh type though, which means they'd still hit the slow path. But I can optimize this by computing an axis-aligned bounding box for each mesh in its local frame and using that for containment tests instead of exact mesh intersection - it's a rough approximation but much faster and should be fine for a 64×64 BEV at 1cm resolution. I could also filter geoms by checking the MuJoCo geom group directly if the naming convention isn't reliable. In robosuite, visual geoms typically have `group=1` and collision geoms have `group=0` (or vice versa). Let me check.

Actually, a much cleaner approach: modify `classify_geom` to also accept and check the geom group, and skip visual geoms. Or add a filter in `build_geom_class_map`.

But the simplest fix is to just optimize the mesh containment. Let me use AABB (oriented bounding box actually - since we transform to local frame, we can use the mesh's local AABB).

Here's my plan:
1. For MESH geoms, compute the AABB from mesh vertices
2. Use `_point_in_box()` with the AABB half-sizes as an approximation
3. This is fast (vectorized numpy) and good enough for occupancy

The cleanest solution is to skip visual geoms (those with `_vis` suffix) when a collision counterpart exists, and use AABB approximation for remaining MESH geoms instead of trimesh ray casting. For the target objects, this means keeping the BOX collision decomposition which is fine for occupancy checks, and for the robot, I can skip all the visual mesh geoms entirely since they're just duplicates of the collision geometry.

import numpy as np

GEOM_PLANE = 0
GEOM_HFIELD = 1
GEOM_SPHERE = 2
GEOM_CAPSULE = 3
GEOM_ELLIPSOID = 4
GEOM_CYLINDER = 5
GEOM_BOX = 6
GEOM_MESH = 7


def _make_grid_points(grid_origin, grid_extent, resolution):
    axes = []
    for d in range(3):
        step = grid_extent[d] / resolution
        axes.append(
            np.linspace(
                grid_origin[d] + step / 2,
                grid_origin[d] + grid_extent[d] - step / 2,
                resolution,
            )
        )
    xx, yy, zz = np.meshgrid(axes[0], axes[1], axes[2], indexing="ij")
    points = np.stack([xx.ravel(), yy.ravel(), zz.ravel()], axis=-1)
    return points, (resolution, resolution, resolution)


def _world_to_local(points, geom_pos, geom_mat):
    mat = geom_mat.reshape(3, 3)
    diff = points - geom_pos[np.newaxis, :]
    local = diff @ mat
    return local


def _point_in_box(local, size):
    return np.all(np.abs(local) <= size[np.newaxis, :], axis=-1)


def _point_in_sphere(local, size):
    r = size[0]
    return np.sum(local ** 2, axis=-1) <= r * r


def _point_in_cylinder(local, size):
    r, h = size[0], size[1]
    xy_dist2 = local[:, 0] ** 2 + local[:, 1] ** 2
    return (xy_dist2 <= r * r) & (np.abs(local[:, 2]) <= h)


def _point_in_capsule(local, size):
    r, h = size[0], size[1]
    r2 = r * r
    xy_dist2 = local[:, 0] ** 2 + local[:, 1] ** 2
    z = local[:, 2]
    in_cyl = (xy_dist2 <= r2) & (np.abs(z) <= h)
    top_d2 = xy_dist2 + (z - h) ** 2
    in_top = (z > h) & (top_d2 <= r2)
    bot_d2 = xy_dist2 + (z + h) ** 2
    in_bot = (z < -h) & (bot_d2 <= r2)
    return in_cyl | in_top | in_bot


def _point_in_ellipsoid(local, size):
    scaled = local / size[np.newaxis, :]
    return np.sum(scaled ** 2, axis=-1) <= 1.0


def _get_mesh_aabb(model, geom_id):
    """Get mesh AABB half-sizes in local frame for fast box approximation."""
    raw = model._model if hasattr(model, '_model') else model
    mesh_id = raw.geom_dataid[geom_id]
    if mesh_id < 0:
        return None
    vert_start = raw.mesh_vertadr[mesh_id]
    vert_count = raw.mesh_vertnum[mesh_id]
    vertices = raw.mesh_vert[vert_start : vert_start + vert_count]
    half_sizes = np.max(np.abs(vertices), axis=0)
    return half_sizes


def build_occupancy_3d(sim, grid_origin, grid_extent, resolution, geom_class_map):
    model = sim.model
    data = sim.data

    points, shape = _make_grid_points(grid_origin, grid_extent, resolution)
    n_pts = points.shape[0]

    semantic = np.zeros(n_pts, dtype=np.uint8)
    binary = np.zeros(n_pts, dtype=bool)

    mesh_aabb_cache = {}

    for geom_id, sem_class in geom_class_map.items():
        geom_type = model.geom_type[geom_id]
        geom_size = model.geom_size[geom_id]
        geom_pos = data.geom_xpos[geom_id]
        geom_mat = data.geom_xmat[geom_id]

        if geom_type == GEOM_BOX:
            bound_r = np.linalg.norm(geom_size)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_SPHERE:
            bound_r = geom_size[0]
        elif geom_type == GEOM_CYLINDER:
            bound_r = np.sqrt(geom_size[0] ** 2 + geom_size[1] ** 2)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_CAPSULE:
            bound_r = geom_size[0] + geom_size[1]
        elif geom_type == GEOM_ELLIPSOID:
            bound_r = np.max(geom_size)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_MESH:
            if geom_id not in mesh_aabb_cache:
                mesh_aabb_cache[geom_id] = _get_mesh_aabb(model, geom_id)
            aabb = mesh_aabb_cache[geom_id]
            if aabb is None:
                continue
            bound_r = np.linalg.norm(aabb)
        else:
            continue

        dists = np.linalg.norm(points - geom_pos[np.newaxis, :], axis=-1)
        candidate_mask = dists <= bound_r * 1.05
        if not np.any(candidate_mask):
            continue

        candidate_pts = points[candidate_mask]
        local = _world_to_local(candidate_pts, geom_pos, geom_mat)

        if geom_type == GEOM_BOX:
            inside = _point_in_box(local, geom_size)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_SPHERE:
            inside = _point_in_sphere(local, geom_size)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_CYLINDER:
            inside = _point_in_cylinder(local, geom_size)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_CAPSULE:
            inside = _point_in_capsule(local, geom_size)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_ELLIPSOID:
            inside = _point_in_ellipsoid(local, geom_size)
        elif geom_type == GEOM_MESH:
            aabb = mesh_aabb_cache[geom_id]
            inside = _point_in_box(local, aabb)
        else:
            continue

        hit_indices = np.where(candidate_mask)[0][inside]
        binary[hit_indices] = True
        upgrade_mask = semantic[hit_indices] < sem_class
        semantic[hit_indices[upgrade_mask]] = sem_class

    semantic = semantic.reshape(shape)
    binary = binary.reshape(shape)

    return semantic, binary

"""
Classify MuJoCo geoms into semantic categories for occupancy labeling.

Categories:
  0 = free (background)
  1 = table
  2 = robot
  3 = target object
"""

import re

FREE = 0
TABLE = 1
ROBOT = 2
TARGET = 3

CATEGORY_NAMES = {FREE: "free", TABLE: "table", ROBOT: "robot", TARGET: "target"}

ROBOT_PATTERNS = [
    r"robot\d*",
    r"gripper",
    r"finger",
    r"link\d*",
    r"hand",
    r"panda",
    r"mount",
]

TABLE_PATTERNS = [
    r"table",
    r"wooden_cabinet",
    r"flat_stove",
    r"cabinet",
    r"stove",
    r"microwave",
    r"fridge",
]

SKIP_PATTERNS = [
    r"wall",
    r"floor",
    r"ground",
    r"arena",
]


def classify_geom(geom_name, body_name, geom_type):
    if geom_name is None:
        geom_name = ""
    if body_name is None:
        body_name = ""

    gn = geom_name.lower()
    bn = body_name.lower()

    if geom_type == 0:
        return None

    # Skip visual-only geoms (collision geoms cover the physical shape)
    if gn.endswith("_vis") or gn.endswith("_visual"):
        return None

    for pat in SKIP_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return None

    if bn == "world":
        return None

    for pat in ROBOT_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return ROBOT

    for pat in TABLE_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, gn) or re.search(pat, bn):
            return TABLE

    return TARGET


def build_geom_class_map(sim):
    """Build geom_id -> semantic_class mapping for all geoms in the model."""
    model = sim.model
    geom_map = {}

    for i in range(model.ngeom):
        geom_name = model.geom_id2name(i)
        body_id = model.geom_bodyid[i]
        body_name = model.body_id2name(body_id)
        geom_type = model.geom_type[i]

        cat = classify_geom(geom_name, body_name, geom_type)
        if cat is not None:
            geom_map[i] = cat

    return geom_map


def print_geom_classification(sim, geom_map):
    """Debug helper: print all geom classifications."""
    model = sim.model
    data = sim.data

    type_names = {
        0: "PLANE", 1: "HFIELD", 2: "SPHERE", 3: "CAPSULE",
        4: "ELLIPSOID", 5: "CYLINDER", 6: "BOX", 7: "MESH",
    }

    for i in range(model.ngeom):
        geom_name = model.geom_id2name(i) or f"unnamed_{i}"
        body_id = model.geom_bodyid[i]
        body_name = model.body_id2name(body_id) or f"body_{body_id}"
        geom_type = model.geom_type[i]
        pos = data.geom_xpos[i]
        cat = geom_map.get(i, None)
        cat_str = CATEGORY_NAMES.get(cat, "SKIP") if cat is not None else "SKIP"
        tname = type_names.get(geom_type, f"UNK({geom_type})")

        print(
            f"g[{i:3d}] {geom_name:45s} body={body_name:35s} "
            f"type={tname:8s} cat={cat_str:8s} "
            f"pos=[{pos[0]:.3f},{pos[1]:.3f},{pos[2]:.3f}]"
        )
